news.title: Mangaluru development body eases land approvals, cuts regularisation fee to 1%
news.para: Mangaluru's property owners rejoice! New government measures have significantly reduced regularisation fees for unauthorised land subdivisions and simplified the approval process for both old and new subdivisions. The necessity for separate land conversion orders in Muda’s master plan has been lifted. To enhance clarity, a public helpdesk is being established at the Muda office, designed to facilitate a smoother approval experience for property owners.

news.title: Mumbai: Dharavi building residents to get 500-sq-ft rehabilitation flats
news.para: Residents of Dharavi are on the brink of transformation through the Dharavi Redevelopment Project. A recent announcement from the state urban development department details the criteria for receiving rehab flats. Each qualifying resident will be allocated a 300 sq-foot space at no charge, with an extra 35% fungible area accessible for some. This strategic project focuses on tackling housing challenges and elevating living conditions in the bustling locality.

news.title: Consumer court orrders Ghaziabad's Krishna Infocom  to refund buyer's money over delay
news.para: The consumer disputes commission has mandated Krishna Infocom to refund Rs 3.7 lakh to Sushma Gupta, who had booked a flat in 2013 but never received possession by the promised January 2020 date. Despite her efforts for resolution, Gupta only received a partial refund of Rs 1 lakh. The ruling against Shyam Builders highlights prevalent issues in property transactions and consumer rights protection within India.

news.title: European property slump deepens as higher borrowing costs force price cuts
news.para: Europe's commercial property landscape is facing mounting pressure as rising borrowing costs complicate debt refinancing endeavors. In fact, quarterly sales have plummeted to their lowest point in three years. To navigate this tough climate, leading investors are adjusting their agreements, often accepting over ten percent price cuts. Notably, several London projects have hit pause due to soaring costs and wavering investor confidence.

news.title: UK lenders approve fewest mortgages since 2023 as borrowing cost rises
news.para: In September 2023, British mortgage approvals plunged to a record low, falling to 53,443 from 54,814 the previous month, driven by escalating borrowing costs. This dip surpassed economists' predictions. Conversely, unsecured lending surged at the fastest pace since 2018, reflecting changing consumer preferences. As mortgage repayments are anticipated to rise steeply over the next five years, affordability worries are mounting, echoed by recent retail sales declines and shifting consumer sentiment.

news.title: HeidelbergCement India's profit falls 33% to ₹16.77 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: During the September quarter, HeidelbergCement India Ltd saw a significant net profit drop of 32.7%, even as its revenue from operations climbed by 10.96% year-over-year. This increase was mainly driven by enhanced sales volumes and better pricing, although the company's total expenses surged by 13.27%, ultimately affecting its profitability. Following the earnings report, shares of the firm declined on the Bombay Stock Exchange.

news.title: Savvy India to add 1.8 million sq ft in GIFT City by July 2027
news.para: Savvy India has around seven million sq ft under development in GIFT City and approximately 2.5 million sq ft of operational space that is fully leased. The company is also expanding beyond residential and commercial real estate into hospitality, GCC offices, industrial warehousing, energy and social infrastructure across Gujarat and Mumbai.

news.title: Maharashtra’s first 3D drone property survey under way in Kolhapur, 40,000 owners to get digital property cards
news.para: Maharashtra has commenced its first-ever 3D GIS drone survey in Kolhapur, covering an area of 4,223 hectares for precise land documentation. This effort aims to digitize maps and provide property cards to around 40,000 owners. Resuming in September, the project utilizes drone technology to capture detailed aerial visuals, with 1.40 lakh images already collected, ensuring enhanced clarity regarding property boundaries.

news.title: Brigade Enterprises’ net profit rises 29% to ₹218.82 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: Brigade Enterprises reports a 28.5% rise in net consolidated profit for the quarter, despite a 12.6% fall in total income. Real estate sales soared to ₹1,827 crore, largely driven by the launch of 2.4 million sq ft of new projects valued at approximately ₹3,000 crore. Positive contributions from leasing and hospitality bolstered their financial standing, with a net worth of ₹6,517.47 crore as of September 30, 2026.

news.title: Delhi civic body's building safety audit may face hurdles
news.para: In an effort to ensure the safety of Delhi’s buildings, the MCD plans a citywide structural safety and fire preparedness audit. Despite highlighting major issues like workforce shortages and budget constraints, they foresee obstacles during inspections in informal settlements and densely populated neighborhoods. The audit will require enhanced technical skills beyond their existing capabilities to evaluate structures adequately.

news.title: Ambuja Cements’ net profit plunges 90% to ₹236 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: Ambuja Cements announced an 89.9 percent decline in net consolidated profit for the quarter ending September 30. The company's total income also decreased by 1.9 percent, indicating challenges in the current market. Cement sales volume during the quarter stood at 16.5 million tonnes, reflecting operational performance. The proposed merger with ACC and Orient has received shareholder support and will move to the National Company Law Tribunal.

news.title: Greenply Industries’ net profit rises 167% to ₹42.72 crore in Q2 FY27
news.para: Greenply Industries has reported an increase in net consolidated profit for the quarter ending September 30, 2026. The company's total income for the second quarter of FY27 rose notably compared to last year’s quarter. In addition to strong financial results, Greenply plans to expand its manufacturing capacity significantly in Uttar Pradesh.

news.title: Ranchi civic body cracks down on illegal buildings in Morabadi, serves notices to 15
news.para: Ranchi Municipal Corporation has taken action by issuing notices to 15 buildings in Morabadi found operating without the required building plans. This decision came after inspections uncovered unauthorized commercial activities within residential areas. The owners now have three days to present the necessary documentation. Additionally, seven other institutions received similar notices due to a lack of proper operational permissions.

news.title: Pune civic body demolishes illegal structures of six RMC plants in Dhayari, citizens want stringent action
news.para: The Pune Municipal Corporation has launched a demolition campaign against illegal ready-mix concrete plants in the Dhayari region. The operation focused on six plants, yet only four were active. Residents voice their concerns, stating that the measures taken are inadequate and demand full closure of these polluting operations.

news.title: Over 700 applications received at Mysuru civic body's e-khata drive
news.para: Mysuru City Corporation conducted a special e-khata drive that received a positive response from applicants. Around 708 applications were submitted across the city’s nine zones during the event. The authorities informed that eligible applications would be processed and completed by a specific timeframe. A second campaign will also take place for those who missed the opportunity due to document deficiencies.

news.title: Don’t issue completion certificates to buildings in aquifer zones: Madras HC tells GCC
news.para: The Madras High Court has mandated the Greater Chennai Corporation to impose strict regulations on Aquifer Recharge Zones, which include Kottivakkam, Palavakkam, and Uthandi. Construction activities in these areas will now be under vigilant scrutiny, highlighting the importance of following the Tamil Nadu Combined Development and Building Rules. A dedicated monitoring committee will be tasked with overseeing development and ensuring all future permits comply with these essential regulations.
